title: Iran Says It's Talking to Oman, Not the U.S., About Reopening a Key Waterway
summary: Have you ever heard of the Strait of Hormuz? It's a narrow waterway in the Middle East where huge oil tankers travel. Lately, Iran has been blocking ships there, causing oil prices to jump. Now, Iran says it's talking with the country of Oman to find a way to let ships through again. But here's the twist: President Trump says the U.S. is negotiating with Iran. Iran says no way — they're only talking to Oman, not America. Trump got angry and called Iran's leaders 'unbelievably duplicitous,' which means he thinks they're saying one thing in public and another in private. He also said the U.S. controls the strait and won't let ships reach Iran unless there's a deal. Over the weekend, Trump said a deal was close and would include reopening the strait and maybe even talks about Iran's nuclear program. But Iran's denial seemed to upset him. The back-and-forth is confusing. Shipping through the strait has already dropped about 28% in just four days, from 71 crossings to 51. Earlier peace talks, helped by other countries, fell apart last month. Trump has often warned of big consequences if Iran doesn't agree, but so far, no final deal has been reached. Some experts think Iran's public statements are meant for its own people, especially hardliners who don't want to give in to the U.S.
why_it_matters: If oil can't move freely through the Strait of Hormuz, the price of gas your family pays could go up, affecting everyday life.

background_read: The Strait of Hormuz is a narrow waterway where about one-fifth of the world's sea-traded oil passes through each day.
Oman, a small country that often helps solve disagreements between other nations, is now talking with Iran (a large Middle Eastern country) about letting ships through again.
The U.S. and Iran have not had official government talks for many years, so when their leaders make claims, it can cause confusion and affect oil prices.
Article_Structure: WHO: Iran, Oman, and President Trump of the United States.
WHAT: Iran says it is negotiating with Oman to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while Trump says the U.S. is negotiating directly.
WHERE: The Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway in the Middle East.
WHY: Because blocked oil tankers are causing oil prices to rise, and both sides want a solution but disagree on who is talking.

perspectives.description: People hoping for peace and stable oil prices are glad that talks are happening, even if it is not clear who is talking.
President Trump believes Iran is being untruthful, and many fear that tensions could lead to military conflict if no deal is reached.
Some analysts point out that both sides often say things for their own public, while behind-the-scenes negotiation may continue.
